summary: This sermon walks through the book of Habakkuk, showing how the prophet brings his complaints and frustrations about injustice directly to God, wrestles with God's unexpected answers, and through a process of questioning, waiting, and listening arrives at a faith that can say 'yet I will rejoice in the Lord' regardless of circumstances.
key_points: Bring your pain and questions directly to God rather than comparing yourself to others
God's judgment is executed on an eternal timeline, not our immediate expectations
After bringing complaints to God, we must wait and listen for His response
The righteous will live by faith, not by understanding everything
Faith to say 'yet' in difficulty is grounded in God's character, past faithfulness, and future promises
big_idea: Our faith to say 'yet I will rejoice in the Lord' in present difficult circumstances is based on God's eternal character, His past faithfulness, and His future promises, even when we don't understand His current actions.
title: The 'Yet' Process
